questions.stem: When should elective surgery be delayed for a patient at risk of airborne infection?
questions.answer: Until the patient is no longer infectious or airborne infection is excluded

questions.stem: For a patient on airborne precautions, which anaesthetic is preferred if possible?
options: General anaesthesia with a tracheal tube
Deep sedation with a supraglottic airway

questions.stem: Which of these counts as an aerosol-generating procedure in anaesthesia?
What should be done first when planning anaesthesia for airborne precautions?
questions.answer: Discuss the plan with the team

questions.stem: What theatre setup is needed for a patient on airborne precautions?
options: Positive pressure theatre with no anteroom
Ward side room with a fan

questions.stem: How should non-disposable equipment be handled on airborne precautions?
options: Share it with other theatres unprotected

questions.stem: What must happen to theatre, equipment and staff after an airborne-precautions case?
Which mask is part of PPE for airborne precautions?
When should high-level PPE be avoided on airborne precautions?
questions.answer: When not needed, outside airway management or other AGPs

questions.stem: What should be done before intubating a patient on airborne precautions?
questions.answer: Have a plan and prepare all equipment beforehand

questions.stem: What protection should staff have during intubation on airborne precautions?
Who should be kept out of the room during intubation on airborne precautions?
Which surgical activities can aerosolise body fluids on airborne precautions?
options: Electrocautery and open or laparoscopic surgery

questions.stem: Has transmission been documented from procedures not involving the respiratory tract?
questions.answer: No, it has not been documented

questions.stem: Name three CPR actions that can aerosolise the virus.
questions.answer: Chest compressions, positive pressure ventilation and intubation
